1-2: A time some hours or minutes later or earlier: when something ends from its start, or starts from its end.
How long something lasts, from its start and its end: in hours or in minutes, or which of two lasts longer.
Sleep across midnight: from a time in the evening to a time in the morning.
A clock that strikes the hours: how many strokes in a few hours.
Two activities one after another, with a break between them.
A watch that is fast or slow by some minutes: the real time from what it shows.
Things done at the same time take no longer: three eggs boiled together in one pot.
Half past, quarter past and quarter to: times said in words, and the minutes in parts of an hour.
A clock face shows every time twice a day: how many times a day it shows a given hour.
A bus that leaves every few minutes: the next one after a given time.
3-4: A time some hours and minutes later or earlier, or the time between two, across the hour.
Minutes in a few hours and a half.
Sleep from a time at night to a time in the morning, on the 24-hour clock.
A clock that strikes the hours and once at every half hour: the strokes in a day.
A watch that loses or gains minutes every hour: what it shows later, or how far a fast and a slow one drift apart.
A bus leaving every few minutes: when the bus of a given number leaves.
A digital clock over a day: how many times it shows a pattern, such as four equal digits.
A school day of lessons with breaks between them: when it ends.
The 24-hour clock and the 12-hour clock: the same moment written both ways.
Minutes and seconds: the times of runners in a race, compared or added.
5-6: Night trips and shifts across midnight: how long one lasts with its breaks, or which of two is longer.
Phoning between time zones: the time at the other end.
A flight across time zones: the local times of take-off and landing.
The hands of a clock on top of each other: how many times in a day, and why not 24.
Two buses on one route, one every 12 minutes and one every 18: when they next leave together.
A film shown twice with a break between: when the second showing ends.
A flight there and back: the time in the air and the difference between the zones.
A watch that gains a few minutes each hour: the true time when it shows a given time.
Two clocks, one gaining and one losing: when they show the same time again.
The angle between the hands of a clock at a given time.
